'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip]]
***[[2025 Gaza City offensive]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] formally launches a ground offensive against [[Hamas]] in [[Gaza City]] as 75 people are killed by Israeli airstrikes, most in Gaza City, with thousands of others evacuating. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-says-gaza-is-burning-it-launches-ground-assault-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
**[[Gaza genocide]]
***An independent [[United Nations]] [[Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory|commission of inquiry]] publishes [https://www.ohchr.org/sites/default/files/documents/hrbodies/hrcouncil/sessions-regular/session60/advance-version/a-hrc-60-crp-3.pdf a report] that "finds that Israel is responsible for the commission of [[genocide]] in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]," listing four of the five genocidal acts defined under international law carried out by [[Israel]] against the [[Palestinian people]] during the war. [https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/09/1165856 (UN News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8641wv0n4go (BBC News)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict]], [[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***[[March 23 Movement|M23]] rebels hold a [[military parade]] of newly-trained recruits in eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese]] towns captured by the rebels in an [[Offensive (military)|offensive]] months prior. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-m23-rebels-rwanda-parade-peace-e9312a2261208eafff0432b7b4159db4 (AP)]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[Israeli attacks on Yemen (May 2025–present)|Israeli attacks on Yemen]]
***The [[Israel Air Force]] bombs at least ten [[Houthis|Houthi]] targets near [[Hudaydah Port]] in [[Al Hudaydah]], [[Yemen]]. The sites targeted by the airstrikes reportedly include a command center and locations used to smuggle weapons from [[Iran]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-867640 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[United States and the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***The [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] approves its first [[United States military aid|weapons aid]] packages for [[Ukraine]]. This is the first use of a new mechanism to [[Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian War|supply Ukraine with weapons]] from U.S. stocks using funds from [[NATO]] countries. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/trump-administration-clears-first-ukraine-arms-aid-paid-by-allies-sources-say-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[War in the Sahel]]
**[[Mali War]]
***[[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]] (JNIM) fighters ambush and burn at least 100 fuel trucks arriving in [[Mali]] from [[Senegal]] and the [[Ivory Coast]]. The attacks are part of a nationwide blockade on fuel and other goods enforced by JNIM as it besieges [[Politics of Mali|Malian government]]-held cities and towns. [https://www.ottumwacourier.com/news/national_news/al-qaida-linked-militants-target-fuel-trucks-in-mali-in-a-blockade-that-could-squeeze/article_4a7730f5-e2f9-5b5e-bc3d-6a2764d23f64.html (AP via ''Ottumwa Courier'')]
*[[Naxalite–Maoist insurgency]]
**The [[Naxalite]]s declare an indefinite unilateral [[ceasefire]] and state their openness to [[peace talks]] with the [[India]]n [[Government of India|government]] amid ongoing [[Operation Green Hunt|military operations]] against their [[insurgency]]. [https://www.ucanews.com/news/indias-maoist-rebels-suspend-armed-struggle/110305 (AFP via UCA News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economy of Uganda]]
**[[Uganda]] announces that it will borrow [[United States dollar|US$]]358 million from the [[African Development Fund]], the [[Arab Bank for Economic Development in Africa]], and [[Standard Chartered]] to fund a [[power grid]] link with [[South Sudan]], a road to the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], and expanded [[Water supply and sanitation in Uganda|clean water access]]. [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/boards-policy-regulation/uganda-borrow-358-million-power-line-south-sudan-other-projects-2025-09-17/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 15 people are killed and 16 others are missing when a [[cloudburst]] causes [[landslide]]s and [[flood]]ing across [[Uttarakhand]], [[India]]. [https://indianexpress.com/article/india/uttarakhand-cloudburst-landslides-floods-killed-missing-10253722/?ref=archive_pg (''The Indian Express'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Climate of Spain]]
**The [[Spain|Spanish]] [[State Meteorological Agency]] announces that 2025 was Spain's hottest summer since records began in 1961, averaging a temperature of {{cvt|24.2|C|F|abbr=on}}, and surpassing 2022's record of {{cvt|24.1|C|F|abbr=on}}. The record-high temperatures caused three [[heatwave]]s over the summer, including the [[2025 European heatwave|16-day heatwave]] in August which sparked [[2025 European and Mediterranean wildfires|wildfires]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/spain-sees-hottest-summer-on-record-in-2025/a-74013753 (DW)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Philippines relations]], [[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea]]
**[[Scarborough Shoal standoff]]
***[[China]]'s [[China Coast Guard|coast guard]] reports that a [[Datu Cabaylo-class multi-mission offshore vessel|''Datu Cabaylo''-class multi-mission offshore vessel]] of the [[Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources|Philippine fisheries bureau]] [[Ramming|rammed]] a [[List of ships of the China Coast Guard|Chinese coast guard vessel]] near the disputed [[Scarborough Shoal]], while the [[Philippines]] say Chinese ships used [[water cannon]]s that damaged the Filipino vessel and injured a crew member. [https://apnews.com/article/philippines-south-china-sea-scarborough-shoal-collision-fc31a170189e4747b8314fb605ca7d0c (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/china-fires-water-cannon-philippine-ships-south-china-sea-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**[[2025 Houthi raids on UN buildings in Sanaa]]
***The [[United Nations]] relocates its [[resident coordinator]]'s office for [[Yemen]] from [[Houthi]]-controlled [[Sanaa]] to [[Presidential Leadership Council|Yemeni government]]-controlled [[Aden]] after the detention of UN staff by the Houthis, while maintaining operations across the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/un-relocates-yemens-resident-coordinators-office-aden-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Australia–Papua New Guinea relations]]
**[[Australia]] announces that it will fund the construction of a new [[National Executive Council|ministerial]] [[Wing (building)|wing]] for [[Papua New Guinea]]'s [[National Parliament House, Port Moresby|Parliament House]] in [[Port Moresby]] as the country marks its 50th anniversary of [[Independence of Papua New Guinea|independence]]. [https://apnews.com/article/papua-new-guinea-independence-celebrations-australia-7790f01cef654f2259f22312836d42cc (AP)]
*[[Hungary–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] restores [[Hungary]]'s full participation in the [[Visa Waiver Program]] after the [[Fifth Orbán Government|Orbán government]] implements measures requested to address security concerns. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-fully-restores-hungarys-status-visa-waiver-program-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mercosur]] signs a [[free trade agreement]] with [[Iceland]], [[Liechtenstein]], [[Norway]], and [[Switzerland]]. [https://apnews.com/article/mercosur-europe-trade-eu-tariffs-640e0a5189a0e5fb882a178608369c16 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020 Beirut explosion]]
**[[Bulgaria]]n [[National Police Service (Bulgaria)|police]] arrest the owner of the ship that brought explosive material to [[Beirut]], [[Lebanon]], which caused an explosion in August 2020 that killed more than 200 people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/bulgaria-arrests-russian-shipowner-relation-deadly-2020-beirut-blast-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Mannheim stabbing]]
**The [[Stuttgart]] [[Oberlandesgericht|Higher Regional Court]] sentences [[Afghans in Germany|Afghan]] national Sulaiman Ataee to [[Life imprisonment in Germany|life in prison]] for the May 2024 [[mass stabbing]] in [[Mannheim]], [[Baden-Württemberg]], [[Germany]], which killed one person and injured five. [https://apnews.com/article/germany-police-killing-mannheim-verdict-ebe0777ce0b6313d5026755830129fd1 (AP)]
*[[Colombian conflict]], [[Kidnappings in Colombia]]
**[[Colombia]]'s [[Special Jurisdiction for Peace]] sentences seven former [[Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia|FARC]] leaders, including ex-[[Military structure of the FARC–EP#Chain_of_command|commander]] [[Timoleón Jiménez]], to up to eight years of [[Reparations (transitional justice)|reparations]] work for their role in [[List of political hostages held by FARC|kidnappings]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250917-colombian-farc-leaders-ordered-to-make-reparations-for-over-21-000-kidnappings (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Controversies surrounding Jair Bolsonaro]]
**A [[Brazil]]ian [[Regional Federal Courts|regional federal court]] orders former [[President of Brazil|president]] [[Jair Bolsonaro]] and the [[Federal government of Brazil|federal government]] to each pay {{FXConvert|BRA|{{#expr:1000000}}|cursign=[[Brazilian real|R$]]}} in [[damages]] for [[Racism in Brazil|racist]] remarks he made in 2021 while [[Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro|in office]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/sep/16/bolsonaro-damages-brazil (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines]]
**The [[Philippine Court of Appeals]] orders the [[Asset freezing|freezing]] of 135 bank accounts and 27 [[insurance policies]] linked to individuals and companies under investigation for alleged [[Corruption in the Philippines|corruption]] in [[flood control]] projects, following a request by the [[Department of Public Works and Highways]] and the [[Anti–Money Laundering Council]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippine-court-freezes-assets-linked-flood-control-project-anomalies-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Killing of Brian Thompson]]
**In the [[United States]], a [[New York (state)|New York]] judge dismisses the two [[Terrorism in the United States|terrorism]] charges brought against [[Luigi Mangione]], the alleged killer of [[UnitedHealthcare]] CEO Brian Thompson, but allows a [[second-degree murder]] charge to stand. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj4y2p8qq5qo (BBC News)]
*[[Modern immigration to the United Kingdom]]
**The [[High Court of Justice]] issues an [[interim injunction]] blocking the deportation of an [[Eritreans|Eritrean]] [[asylum seeker]] to [[France]] under a [[Return migration|returns agreement]], pending a hearing on his [[Human trafficking in the United Kingdom|trafficking]] claim. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/16/uk-court-temporarily-blocks-deportation-of-eritrean-asylum-seeker (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Murder of Agnes Wanjiru]]
**[[Kenya]]'s [[Magistrates' Court (Kenya)|Magistrates' Court]] issues an [[arrest warrant]] and seeks the [[extradition]] of a [[British people|British citizen]] over the 2012 murder of [[Kenyan people|Kenyan]] woman Agnes Wanjiru near a [[British Army Training Unit Kenya|British army training camp]] in [[Nanyuki]], [[Laikipia County]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/kenya-issues-arrest-warrant-uk-citizen-murder-case-blamed-soldiers-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Nord Stream pipelines sabotage]]
**An [[Italy|Italian]] [[Judiciary of Italy|appellate court]] approves the extradition to [[Germany]] of a [[Ukrainians|Ukrainian]] national allegedly involved in the 2022 [[Nord Stream]] [[pipeline]] explosions. The suspect's lawyer says that he plans to appeal the decision to the [[Supreme Court of Cassation (Italy)|Supreme Court of Cassation]]. [https://apnews.com/article/italy-germany-pipleine-explosion-extradition-2db1be82baa27a41ac7d8e83a8c17643 (AP)]
*[[Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse]]
**[[Serbia]]n prosecutors indict former [[Ministry of Construction, Transport, and Infrastructure (Serbia)|construction minister]] [[Goran Vesić]] and 12 others on public safety charges over the [[Novi Sad railway station]] roof collapse that killed 16 people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/serbia-indicts-13-railway-station-roof-collapse-that-killed-16-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Romania]]n prosecutors indict former [[President of Romania|presidential]] candidate [[Călin Georgescu]] and 21 others on charges of attempting to undermine national security by planning violent protests after the cancellation of the [[2024 Romanian presidential election|2024 election]] over [[Accusations of Russian interference in the 2024 Romanian presidential election|alleged Russian interference]]. [https://www.ft.com/content/5248339f-3dcc-4ee3-b2b3-7b54e4ecf0bc (''Financial Times'')]
*[[Senegal]]ese authorities intercept 112 [[Gambia]]n migrants aboard a [[pirogue]] off the coast of [[Dakar]] on the suspicion of [[irregular migration]] as they attempt to [[African immigration to Europe|reach Europe]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/senegal-intercepts-pirogue-carrying-112-migrants-attempting-atlantic-crossing-2025-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*The [[High courts of South Korea|Seoul Central District Court]] issues an arrest warrant for former [[People Power Party]] floor leader [[Kweon Seong-dong]] on charges of receiving [[Corruption in South Korea|illegal political funds]] from the [[Unification Church]] during the [[2022 South Korean presidential election]] campaign. [https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10577045 (''The Korea Herald'')]
*The [[Gauteng Division of the High Court of South Africa|high court]] in [[Gauteng]], [[South Africa]], rejects an appeal by the family of former [[President of Zambia|Zambian president]] [[Edgar Lungu]], upholding its ruling that Lungu's remains must be returned to [[Zambia]] for burial. [https://apnews.com/article/zambia-edgar-lungu-south-africa-burial-ruling-db3ffc3ee61ee40832112971e0566f18 (AP)]
*[[U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] files a $15 billion [[defamation]] lawsuit against the newspaper ''[[The New York Times]]'' after the paper published articles and a book alleging that part of [[The Trump Organization]]'s wealth was acquired through [[fraud]]. [https://www.npr.org/2025/09/16/nx-s1-5543030/donald-trump-nytimes-lawsuit (NPR)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Malawian general election]]
**[[Malawi]]ans vote to elect a [[President of Malawi|president]], the 229 members of the [[National Assembly (Malawi)|National Assembly]], and 509 [[Politics of Malawi#Local government|local government]] councillors. [https://apnews.com/article/election-malawi-president-parliament-africa-chakwera-397aa544946efd6e1dfc0258d406bfdf (AP)]
*[[Internet in Afghanistan]]
**[[Afghanistan|Afghan]] [[Supreme Leader of Afghanistan|supreme leader]] [[Hibatullah Akhundzada]] orders a complete ban on [[Wi-Fi]] [[internet]] in the northern [[Balkh Province]] to "prevent [[Morality in Islam|immorality]]". [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/taliban-balkh-afghan-jalalabad-b2827557.html (''The Independent'')]
*Matteo Rossi and [[Lorenzo Bugli]] are elected the new [[captains regent]] of [[San Marino]] for the following semester. [https://www.sanmarinortv.sm/news/politica-c2/eletti-i-capitani-reggenti-per-il-prossimo-semestre-saranno-matteo-rossi-e-lorenzo-bugli-a280382 (''San Marino RTV'')]
